Two clubs would be relegated and 2 teams promoted from [[Thailand Division 1 League]]. The team that finished in 8th position would play in a relegation play-off. The official name of the league at this time was '''GSM Thai League'''. [[Krung Thai Bank FC|Krung Thai Bank]] won their first ever Thai Premier League title and their 5th major title at the time. ==Member clubs== *[[Bangkok Bank FC|Bangkok Bank]] *[[Bangkok Christian College FC|Bangkok Christian College]] (''promoted from [[Thailand Division 1 League|Division 1]]'') *[[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] *[[Chula-Sinthana FC|Sinthana]] *[[Krung Thai Bank FC|Krung Thai Bank]] *[[Osotsapa FC|Osotsapa M-150]] *[[Port Authority of Thailand FC|Port Authority of Thailand]] *[[Royal Thai Air Force FC|Royal Thai Air Force]] *[[Thailand Tobacco Monopoly FC|Thailand Tobacco Monopoly]] *[[TOT FC|TOT]] {{location map+ |Thailand |float=right |width=350 |caption=Locations of the Thai Premier League 2002–03 teams |places= {{Location map~ |Thailand|marksize=11 |lat=13.746323 |long=100.527413 |label='''Bangkok''' |position=right}} {{Location map~ |India |mark=TransparentPlaceholder.png |marksize=2 |lat=17.5 |long=83.0 |label_size=80|label='''Bangkok teams'''

They defeated [[TOT FC|TOT]] 1-0 in the final. ==Asian Representation== * In a revamped [[2002–03 AFC Champions League|Asian Champions League]], [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] would surprise the whole of Asia and bring back past glories not seen since [[Thai Farmers Bank FC|Thai Farmers Bank]] in the mid 1990s and would reach the final of the Champions League where they would come runners up to UAE side [[Al Ain]]. On their way to the final BEC would claim victories over old Japanese rivals [[Kashima Antlers]], [[Shanghai Shenhua]] of China, [[Daejeon Citizen]] of South Korea and Uzbekistan side [[Pakhtakor Tashkent]]. * This was also the first time that two Thai clubs would enter the Champions League. [[Osotsapa FC|Osotsapa]] would also take part but would find the going tough and would crash out in embarrassing circumstances in the group stage. * [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] would also take part in the newly formed [[2003 ASEAN Club Championship]] to be held in [[Indonesia]] against the best of the rest of the ASEAN and SAFF region. Here they made the final but got beat by Indian side [[Kingfisher East Bengal FC|Kingfisher East Bengal]] ==Annual awards== ===Coach of the Year=== *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Narong Suwannachote]] - [[Krung Thai Bank FC|Krung Thai Bank]] ===Player of the year=== *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Khampee Pintapol]] - [[Bangkok Bank FC|Bangkok Bank]] ===Top scorer=== *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Sarayoot Chaikamdee]] 12 Goals[[Football records in Thailand]] - [[Port Authority of Thailand FC|Port Authority of Thailand]] ==Champions== The league champion was [[Krung Thai Bank F.C.|Krung Thai Bank]]. ==References== {{Reflist}} *[https://www.rsssf.org/tablest/thai03.html Thailand 2002-03] RSSSF ==External links== *[https://web.archive.org/web/20080913070725/http://www.thaifootballleague.com/ Official Website] {{S-start}} {{Succession box|title=[[Thai Premier League]]|before=[[2001–02 Thai League|Thai League
